solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plant sadly laid off dozens to begin with

indicators.note: something that goes sadly goes wrong, so the letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

indicators.note: what comes to begin with is the opening letter of the word

parts.note: the opening letter of dozens

explanation.surface: A gardener sadly lays off staff, dozens of them at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid off' reads as losing jobs, but it is simply seven letters to shuffle, with the D from dozens added.
explanation.definitionFit: The daffodil is a yellow spring bulb flower, a familiar example of a garden plant.

clue.text: Cowardly, to cry out in pain

parts.note: to yell is to cry out loudly
what someone says when in pain

explanation.surface: Someone who cries out at the first twinge of pain is called a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: The cry of pain is the exclamation OW, which is added after the shout.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is an informal colour term for a person lacking courage, as in 'yellow-bellied'.

clue.text: Well-ventilated eagle's nest, as some would say

indicators.note: what people would say is what is heard, so the spoken form matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: an eyrie is the high nest of an eagle, which some pronounce like this answer

explanation.surface: An eagle's nest high on a crag must be a breezy spot.
explanation.walkthrough: EYRIE has several pronunciations, so 'some' covers those who say it to rhyme with 'hairy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A room with plenty of fresh air circulating through it is described as airy, meaning spacious and breezy.

clue.text: Setter's regrettably served up highly seasoned sausage

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means going upward, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: the setter speaks of himself, and setter's is setter is, so I'M
alas is an exclamation of regret

explanation.surface: The setter apologises for having served a spicy sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the setter refers to themselves as I or ME, so 'Setter's' becomes I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured Italian sausage strongly flavoured with garlic and spices.

clue.text: Window of no great significance seen around Kentucky

indicators.note: something seen around another thing surrounds it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: slight means small or unimportant
KY is the US postal abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: An unremarkable window is spotted somewhere in Kentucky.
explanation.walkthrough: US state postal codes are fair game in crosswords, and here one splits the word for unimportant after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A skylight is a window set into a roof or ceiling to let daylight in.

clue.text: Look fixedly on old boy going round summerhouse

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily

indicators.note: going round means turning about, so the letters face the other way

parts.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Someone stares at an old boy walking round a garden summerhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the gazing above the reversed old boy in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small open garden pavilion, the kind of structure also called a summerhouse.

clue.text: Reportedly transmitted small sum of money

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how the word is heard

parts.note: transmitted means dispatched, which is pronounced the same as the coin

explanation.surface: A news item about a tiny sum of money being wired somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words sound alike though they are spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A cent is a hundredth of a dollar or euro, a coin worth very little.

clue.text: Uncle Sam, a graduate touring Morecambe, perhaps

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a touring party travels all around a place, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a Master of Arts is a graduate
Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, one of Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: An American and a university graduate travel round the Lancashire seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the seaside town, but 'perhaps' asks for a person with that surname: the comedian Eric Morecambe.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam is the cartoon personification of the United States government and nation.

clue.text: Rascal, the last to back church body

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of back
the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: A rascal is the final person anyone would want supporting the church council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as the verb support, but it is the word whose last letter is taken; 'church body' reads as a governing council but is part of a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is an old-fashioned word for a dishonest, unprincipled rogue.

clue.text: Young female horse sick in outskirts of Fowey

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it
the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the outer letters are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of Fowey
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A young mare has fallen ill on the edge of the Cornish town of Fowey.
explanation.walkthrough: Fowey is a harbour town in Cornwall; only its two outer letters are wanted, with ILL between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A filly is a female foal or young mare, usually under four years old.

clue.text: The last word about the Italian teacher's first complaint

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: amen is the word said at the end of a prayer
il is Italian for the

indicators.note: first points to the opening position, so only the leading letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher's principal grievance is that the Italian always has the last word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' looks like a grumble, but here it means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness or disorder, which is exactly what an ailment is.

clue.text: Residence containing old cylindrical rods

indicators.note: a thing containing another holds it inside

parts.note: a dwelling is a place of residence
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An old house has been built around a framework of wooden rods.
explanation.walkthrough: The O goes in straight after the first letter of the home.
explanation.definitionFit: Dowelling is round wooden or metal rod stock, cut into pegs for joining pieces of furniture.

clue.text: Lacking energy and ill-prepared for shopping?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read whimsically: going to the shops without the paper you wrote your purchases on

explanation.surface: Someone tired and flat heads to the shops without having planned what to buy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning is a joke reading, splitting the word into 'list' plus '-less'.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless is the ordinary word for feeling sluggish and lacking any enthusiasm or drive.

clue.text: Your and my period of time on radio

indicators.note: on radio, words are only heard and never seen, so the pronunciation counts

parts.note: an hour is a period of sixty minutes, and its H is silent

explanation.surface: A radio slot described as belonging to you and me.
explanation.walkthrough: Because the H of hour is silent, it sounds just like the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive word for something belonging jointly to the speaker and the listener combines 'your' and 'my'.

clue.text: Get a rule prepared to adjust

indicators.note: something prepared has been made up or worked into shape, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to draw up a rule in order to fix something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared' looks like it describes the rule, but it tells you to shuffle the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To regulate a machine or process is to control and set it so it works properly.

clue.text: Supporter of Liverpool primarily, say

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter is the one kept

parts.note: the opening letter of Liverpool
e.g. is the abbreviation meaning for example, just as say can

explanation.surface: A Liverpool football fan, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter of Liverpool' wants to be a football fan; the definition is 'Supporter' alone, meaning something that holds weight up.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg supports a body or a table, so it is literally something that bears weight.

clue.text: Name of titled woman in Gilbert and Sullivan originally

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it
originally points to the origin, the beginning of each word, so the opening letters are kept

parts.note: the opening letter of Gilbert
Lady is the title of a peer's wife or daughter
the opening letter of Sullivan

explanation.surface: Asking the name of an aristocratic heroine in a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan wrote Victorian comic operettas full of titled ladies; here they supply only their initials, which wrap around the lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladys is a woman's first name, so it is simply an example of a name.

clue.text: Frightening bird crossing entrance to track

indicators.note: crossing a thing means spanning it from side to side, so one piece stretches over the other

parts.note: the starling is a common speckled songbird

indicators.note: the entrance is the way in, the very start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of track

explanation.surface: A scary bird flies across the gateway to a racetrack.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird is split after its fourth letter to let the T in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something startling gives a sudden shock or scare, so it is alarming or frightening.

clue.text: Choral composition put worker possibly on edge

indicators.note: in a down answer, one thing on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a worker ant is one example of a worker
a hem is the finished edge of cloth

explanation.surface: A piece of choral music puts a working singer on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On edge' reads as nervous, but it is positional: the insect sits above the border in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a piece of sacred music for choir, usually with words from scripture.

clue.text: Popular act? Absolutely

parts.note: what is in is fashionable and popular
a deed is an act

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a stage act is popular and is told yes, completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular act' looks like a crowd-pleasing performer, but act here is a deed done.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words serve as emphatic agreement, an enthusiastic 'yes' or 'certainly' in reply.

clue.text: Bright red mark from very minor injury?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the vivid red colour

definitions.note: a whimsical noun reading, whereas the answer is normally an adjective
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read whimsically: a scar with the diminutive ending -let, like piglet or booklet, is a tiny scar

explanation.surface: A vivid red mark left by a minor scrape.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a made-up word: -let makes things small, so a little scar would be a scar-let.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is the name of a brilliant red colour, slightly tinged with orange.

clue.text: Break cooking vessels when climbing

indicators.note: in a down answer, climbing means going upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: pans are vessels used for cooking

explanation.surface: Someone smashes the pots and pans while clambering about the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Read upward in this down answer, the kitchenware spells a new word.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap something is to break it suddenly and cleanly, often with a sharp crack.

clue.text: Exemplary learner follows fashion

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so this piece is placed second

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style
L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A model pupil keeps up with the latest fashions.
explanation.walkthrough: The learner comes after the fashion word even though it appears first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A model pupil or citizen is one who serves as a perfect example for others.

clue.text: No more than a lake

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a small lake or pond, common in English place names

explanation.surface: Dismissing a body of water as nothing more than a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for a lake survives in English place names such as Windermere.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means only or nothing but; as a noun it is an old word for a small lake or pond.

clue.text: Heading off, tiny child initially sees spectacular chasm

indicators.note: with its head taken off, a word loses its first letter

parts.note: a baby is a very small child

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of sees
the opening letter of spectacular

explanation.surface: A toddler heading off on a trip first sees a spectacular gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' reads as setting out, but it means removing the first letter; 'initially' serves both following words.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a deep, seemingly bottomless gorge or pit, the same thing as a chasm.

clue.text: Serious alteration to sneer at

indicators.note: an alteration changes the form of something, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A grave change of attitude towards someone you mock.
explanation.walkthrough: The mocking phrase is only letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone earnest is sincere and intensely serious in manner, without levity.
